title: QUIC internal server 0-RTT opening work item
summary: Add the smallest internal managed-server early-data path that advertises QUIC early_data, accepts only same-listener admitted PSKs, opens server ZeroRtt packets, and delivers bounded STREAM/PING/PADDING early data.
planned_changes:
- Add internal server early-data enablement behind managed resumption tickets.
- Emit TLS NewSessionTicket early_data with the QUIC sentinel max_early_data_size value only when remembered 0-RTT transport parameters exist.
- Emit ClientHello early_data when a detached ticket has early-data prerequisite material while keeping pre_shared_key last.
- Compose server early-data acceptance with validated PSK binder state and the REQ-QUIC-CRT-0152 listener-local admission gate.
- Publish server ZeroRtt open material and EncryptedExtensions early_data only after admission succeeds.
- Add a server establishing-phase ZeroRtt packet opener and bounded STREAM/PING/PADDING runtime delivery path.
- Reject forbidden 0-RTT ACK, CRYPTO, NEW_TOKEN, and HANDSHAKE_DONE frames.
- Add focused positive, negative, fuzz-shaped tests and a benchmark lane for server ZeroRtt opening.
- Preserve public API, IsSupported, HTTP/3, and interop zerortt inventory classification.
verification_plan: Run focused REQ_QUIC_CRT_0153 tests first, then the nearby REQ_QUIC_CRT_0149 through REQ_QUIC_CRT_0153 homes, SpecTrace core validation, Release build, full Release tests, and diff whitespace checks.
completion_notes: The managed server now has an internal early-data path that can advertise QUIC early_data, accept a zero-length ClientHello early_data offer only after same-listener PSK validation and listener-local admission, publish server ZeroRtt open material, open Version 1 ZeroRtt packets, and deliver bounded STREAM/PING/PADDING payloads to the stream registry. Disabled early data and replayed tickets do not publish server ZeroRtt material. Forbidden ACK frames in 0-RTT trigger a local protocol violation. Public API, IsSupported, HTTP/3, external anti-replay coordination, and interop zerortt support classification remain unchanged.
